source: XIP-4 (HX1) handshake vectors, generated by contrib/testgen/gen_hx1_handshake_vectors.py from the test framework (test/functional/test_framework/v2_p2p.py). Each input is SHA-256 of 'XIP-4 test vector: ' followed by its name (garbage truncated); ell_initiator and ell_responder are secp256k1_ellswift_create(priv, aux). Application packet i has the contents 'I->R' or 'R->I' followed by i as 4 bytes little-endian; 226 are sent each way, and entries pin application packets 0, 1, 223, 224, 225 plus every decoy. In a hybrid session the responder's stage-2 stream starts with its confirmation packet (stage-2 index 0, a decoy with empty contents), so its application packet i has stage-2 index i + 1. All sha256 fields are SHA-256.

mlkem768.description: FIPS 203 KeyGen_internal(d, z) and Encaps_internal(ek, m) for the inputs above, and Decaps of ct with bit 0 of byte 0 flipped (implicit rejection, J(z || ct'))

handshakes.name: V1
handshakes.description: mainnet, both sides in prefer mode, no decoys other than the responder's confirmation packet (its first stage-2 packet, a decoy with empty contents sent right after it switches to stage 2)

handshakes.name: V2
handshakes.description: testnet A, same inputs as V1

handshakes.name: V4
handshakes.description: mainnet, same inputs as V1, with decoys: the responder sends one before VP_R (it carries garbage_R as associated data); the initiator sends two before VP_I (the first carries garbage_I) and one stage-2 decoy right after VP_I

handshakes.name: V5
handshakes.description: mainnet, a prefer-mode initiator meets a classical (mode 0) responder: both version packets are empty and the session stays on the stage-1 keys

bad_encapsulation_keys.description: V6: V1's ek with one coefficient out of range; an initiator that receives either in an otherwise valid OFFER must disconnect without sending VP_I
